records.region: Washoe County, western Nevada, United States: McClellans Creek, the Cottonwood Creek alluvial valley, Mullen Creek and the southern-to-central Pyramid Lake receiving basin.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative named receiving-river system; different upper tributaries, ice, lake and lower branches retain separate component identities.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative receiving-creek identity for the complete selected McClellans Creek–Cottonwood Creek–Mullen Creek composite and its continuation into Pyramid Lake. The name is supported on the downstream landward receiving creek; it is not a scalar renaming of the distinct upper tributaries or the lake interior.
records.completion_scope: All 15 original parts and 89 stored positions were compared with the regional original map and overlapping unmarked southern/northern crops, using separate private orientation aids. The opening tributary, full alluvial valley, marsh junction, named receiving creek, shore entry and complete lake-interior extension have ordinary geographic support. No necessary through-link remains unresolved.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative receiving-creek identity for the complete selected McClellans Creek–Cottonwood Creek–Mullen Creek composite and its continuation into Pyramid Lake. The name is supported on the downstream landward receiving creek; it is not a scalar renaming of the distinct upper tributaries or the lake interior.

scope_limits: The selected opening is not established as a natural headwater.
Intermittent-channel mapping and a broad alluvial floor do not establish year-round surface flow or current water-routing details.
Mullen Creek is a representative receiving-system candidate; McClellans Creek, Cottonwood Creek and Pyramid Lake retain their own component identities.
The long lake-interior continuation is a modeled selected extension, not an observed river channel or lake-current survey.
No formal registry verification or whole-feature scalar/Korean name is asserted.

bounded_name_candidates.name: Machmell River
bounded_name_candidates.support: BC Parks names the Machmell, Genesse and Neechanz confluence as the beginning of a deltaic freshwater wetland, and describes Machmell as a river. The selected lower braided/delta landscape is geographically compatible.
bounded_name_candidates.limit: Compatibility with an unnamed photographic corridor is not treated as proof that this selected line is the named Machmell. The prose contains no selected-reach coordinates, named receiving-lake statement or independently inspected label placement. Genesse and Neechanz names are not transferred to visible branches.

records.region: Chihuahua, eastern desert-wash corridor and receiving playa northeast of the state capital
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The successfully read imagery establishes the physical corridor but contains no name labels. The bounded discovery pass did not establish an independent source directly naming the selected river or its receiving system. Incidental matches to held publications, nearby place names, other drainages, basin-only tables and uninspected borrowed cartography do not supply naming evidence.
records.geographic_disambiguation: All 16 selected parts have complete ordinary geographic correspondence from an eastern desert wash through its southwest bend and west/northwest alluvial corridor to the receiving playa. The inspected photographic source supplies no hydronym, and the bounded independent naming search supplied no direct naming evidence. This is a completed null-name scope hold; inherited source restrictions remain separate.
records.completion_scope: Complete connected desert-wash, valley/alluvial-floor and receiving-playa correspondence, including all stored parts and joins. Source endpoint, rendered endpoint and separately stored quantized final position are retained in their supplied forms. No supported representative river-system name, accepted scalar name, Korean name, formal registry determination or application is claimed.
records.supported_name_scope: The successfully read imagery establishes the physical corridor but contains no name labels. The bounded discovery pass did not establish an independent source directly naming the selected river or its receiving system. Incidental matches to held publications, nearby place names, other drainages, basin-only tables and uninspected borrowed cartography do not supply naming evidence.

scope_limits: No supported hydronym is attached to the selected river, a component reach or the receiving playa. Discovery names and search excerpts are not substantive evidence.

The generalized selected line does not trace every visible darker wash, bend or bank. Local offsets remain within the same connected valley/alluvial floor; no present flow or exact bank alignment is claimed.

Some lower-floor areas show rectangular surface patterns and tracks. These are geographic context only; current cultivation, hydraulic structures, irrigation operation or engineered diversion is not established.
Dry-looking wash and playa surfaces are sufficient for ordinary geographic correspondence. Perennial water, present flow and precise shorelines remain unverified.
The source and render terminal fields coincide but remain separately preserved, as does the quantized final stored position. No endpoint was moved to the playa centre or a present water edge.
Individual imagery scene dates and formal naming-register status remain unverified.

records.region: Southern Chugach Mountains near Valdez, Alaska, United States: Deserted Glacier and its northgoing foreland corridor, Lowe River valley and lower braidplain, and the Port Valdez receiving coast.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative named receiving-river system; different upper tributaries, ice, lake and lower branches retain separate component identities.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative named receiving-river system for the complete Deserted Glacier/foreland–Lowe River–lower braidplain composite to Port Valdez. The candidate does not rename the glacier, infer a name for its unlabelled foreland feeder, or turn each selected lower braidplain segment into the same exact modern channel.
records.completion_scope: All 32 original parts and 106 stored positions were compared with the original regional map and overlapping unmarked eastern, middle and western crops, plus the original endpoint crop and separate orientation aids. The complete glacial opening, foreland transfer, Lowe valley, canyon, lower braidplain/slough and distinct source/render tidal endings are supported at ordinary corridor scale. No necessary geographic link remains unresolved.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative named receiving-river system for the complete Deserted Glacier/foreland–Lowe River–lower braidplain composite to Port Valdez. The candidate does not rename the glacier, infer a name for its unlabelled foreland feeder, or turn each selected lower braidplain segment into the same exact modern channel.

scope_limits: The source cartography does not establish current glacier-front position, a named natural source, ice-surface routing or year-round flow along every selected segment.
The foreland feeder is geographically supported but its own hydronym is unestablished.
The lower selection includes the common braidplain and Canyon Slough setting; precise contemporary channel membership and flow distribution are not verified.
The original-source and rendered endpoints differ slightly but share the supported tidal-mouth setting; exact present coastline matching is not claimed.
No formal registry verification or whole-feature scalar/Korean name is asserted.

bounded_name_observations.role: Directly labelled southern glacial component; an upstream ice feature, not the river-system representative.

bounded_name_observations.name: Lowe River
bounded_name_observations.role: Repeatedly labelled receiving river across the upper valley, canyon, lower braidplain and tidal approach; representative system candidate.

bounded_name_observations.name: Canyon Slough
bounded_name_observations.role: Named southern lower-braidplain watercourse beside and within the common Lowe receiving corridor; bounded component observation.

bounded_name_observations.name: Port Valdez
bounded_name_observations.role: Named tidal/coastal receiver at the selected western ending; not an alternative river name.
